title: The Rank Property of Thin Slabs: exact rank at most 2b for the far-field blocks of the reduced slab-interface matrix
author: Anna Yesypenko, Per-Gunnar Martinsson
work: SlabLU: A Two-Level Sparse Direct Solver for Elliptic PDEs
difficulty_reason: The counted proof is the article’s own theoretical justification of the two-level solver and is not a qualification exercise. Starting from the Schur complement T_11 = A_11 - A_12 A_22^{-1} A_21 of the slab-ordered five-point stencil, the author must exhibit the block LDU factorization of the sparse banded matrix A_22, propagate the sparsity pattern of A_F2 and A_2B through the triangular factors U_22^{-1} and L_22^{-1} to obtain the factorizations X_F2 = [A_Fa 0 A_Fg] U_22^{-1} and Y_2B = L_22^{-1} [0; A_bB; A_gB], conclude that the compensation term X_Fg Y_gB has exact rank |J_gamma| = 2b because the middle column block of X_F2 vanishes identically, and finally separate the sparse O(1)-entry part A_FB from that rank-2b part, with the symmetric argument for (T_11)_BF. Supplying the definitions of the slab interface, the buffer b and the Schur-complement blocks does not turn this into a routine exercise: the rank certificate for a nested-dissection Schur complement is the source-local structural result on which the whole solver rests, and it is above ordinary PhD qualifying level in numerical linear algebra.
